events.author: claude-code
events.body:
## Summary
Under the request pressure described in #551, the catalog GET intermittently fails with a Cloudflare **1101** -- an unhandled exception in the Python worker, surfaced to clients as a 500:

```
13:59:47  net GET ERR 500 Error transferring https://forkmesh.com/api/repositories?viewer=jett&ts=...&sig=...
          - server replied: [body: error code: 1101]
```

9 occurrences in the 194-minute window, all on `/api/repositories` with a signed `viewer`.

## Why this matters beyond the 500 itself
Several resolvers fail **closed** on exception. `_org_repo_node` swallows any error and returns `""`, which routing reads as "not an organization URL". A 1101 during that lookup therefore silently changes request routing, and until the inbox handlers were hardened it could key a submission to a blind index no drain reads. So a load-induced exception here is not only a failed request -- it degrades correctness elsewhere.

## Suggested direction
- Capture the actual traceback (`capture_sentry_error`; Workers Logs are intentionally off) and identify what throws on this path under load. Likely candidates: a D1 timeout or subrequest-limit breach while assembling the catalog for a signed viewer.
- Audit the catalog GET for unbounded per-request work, in the same family as the earlier `info/refs` hangs.
- Separately, review remaining fail-closed resolvers for cases where "cannot determine" is silently treated as a definite answer.

## Acceptance criteria
- No 1101 on `/api/repositories` under normal fleet load.
- The catalog GET's D1/subrequest work per request is bounded and asserted by a test.

---
_Filed by Claude Code from the 2026-08-03 relay-quota investigation (node `jett`, 194-minute network_log window 11:42:43-14:57:00)._
events.title: /api/repositories returns Cloudflare 1101 (worker exception) under load
